prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Marlinstone forecasts intents/performance-history. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module recalculates Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector constraints upon configuration/weather/staffing/workload changes. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;Pushback Window Token at freeze. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Halcyon reviews/publication-confirms;Saffron confirms pre-freeze;Aircraft Operator Representative reviews timing;changes justified. Foxglove read-only except coordination-roles. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones(refresh≤5s/validated-event);Adapter→Skylark/Ironleaf:occupancy/equipment-status. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities. Gate Conflict Detector checks adjacent-stand resequencing before broader delays;compares arrivals/departures/gates/towing/published-stand-status. Handling Resource Planner compares added-handling-resource relief against flow measures. Lantern distributes equipment/apron-congestion advisories within Business Rules

New part:
S474: The Surface Surveillance Adapter verifies that the apron position is physically clear, while the East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor provide supporting movement evidence for the reopened area.
S475: The Tower Supervisor is advised only when the gate or stand decision changes runway sequence assumptions, expected taxi duration, or a departure metering commitment.
S476: The Aircraft Operator Representative confirms whether the aircraft can accept a revised stand assignment without disrupting maintenance release, fueling sequence, boarding control, or cabin readiness.
S477: The Handling Resource Planner estimates whether the proposed turnaround can be recovered using available loading teams, passenger stairs, boarding bridges, cleaning crews, and baggage transfer resources.
S478: The Airline Interface Adapter maintains airline-provided connection exposure, including protected passengers, minimum connection time pressure, and groups that require assisted transfer.
S479: The Regional Flow Manager balances passenger connection pressure against network fairness when a gate recovery action would improve one bank of departures but consume scarce apron capacity.
S480: The Network Operations Liaison reviews whether protecting a connecting passenger group supports wider network recovery or only transfers delay to a later sector.
S481: The Slot Coordinator protects constrained rotations by checking that a recovered gate plan remains compatible with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time and any slot compliance expectation.
S482: The Target Off Block Time is revised only when the actor responsible for the turnaround confirms that the boarding, servicing, and ramp movement assumptions are achievable.
S483: The Departure Metering Service sequences recovered departures so that aircraft released from delayed turnarounds do not create a new surface queue at the runway holding points.
S484: Sector Load Monitor produces the Departure Fix Load Sheet when projected recovered departures require a consolidated view of demand by departure fix.
S485: The Airport CDM Portal shows downstream departure-fix pressure as contextual information for gate recovery decisions, without allowing the stand plan to override accepted airspace constraints.
S486: The Business Rules Registry holds the local rules for connection protection, gate compatibility, towing priority, stand reopening approval, and minimum turnaround recovery margins.
S487: The Collaborative Decision Log records each accepted conflict resolution with the chosen stand, rejected alternatives, affected passenger connections, and the rationale used by the responsible actor.
S488: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the same decision history for later traceability, including manual overrides, timestamp corrections, and identity of the approving role.
S489: The Performance Analytics Warehouse measures whether recovered gate assignments reduced missed connections, reduced secondary stand conflicts, and improved aircraft rotation stability during the Recovery Phase.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
